why: Linux keeps 15 bytes of a process name. The implant's is longer, so ps shows it cut short and a whole-name comparison never matches. Observed in the sandbox, not assumed: a binary run under the full name appears as the first 15 bytes. The shell check compares whole names and has therefore never matched on Linux. A name of exactly 15 bytes that begins a longer implant name is that implant.

findings.match: an implant process is running now
